### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **73** documentable anchor(s).

**50** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 33 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d91ee7c331befa42f62f72575ffd883ca979688e` — the merge of head `d453ea50d7f894e4bf451b51778df0a952f8500c` into base `55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d91ee7c331befa42f62f72575ffd883ca979688e && git checkout d91ee7c331befa42f62f72575ffd883ca979688e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6 d453ea50d7f894e4bf451b51778df0a952f8500c && git checkout -B drift-repro 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6 && git merge --no-ff d453ea50d7f894e4bf451b51778df0a952f8500c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `92bda9e9dd0ebc0b2f02962003ab99ed66c97c67`
Local-runs: none

PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#22863 (stage 6b-2-pre of #15204, branch `claude/issue-15204-s6b2pre-grant-by-name`, base `main` at `55382dc02a`), read as the net diff against `main` at the head above: 91 files, +833 / −1,860. Judged against seat answer 6109520247 (Q1 → A, the stage this PR builds), the stage-8 measurement 6110720794 and its seat answer 6110777865 (E2), and ADR-0131 D4 / D10 as the record the stage executes. Read-only: the diff, the card's body and comments, the head's check-runs; nothing built, run or re-run.

**The stage's three sentences (6109520247, Q1 → A), each against the diff:**

1. "every grant writer stores the set's machine name only" — **met.** The five writers the 6b-2 stop named write `{ permission_set: name }` and read no `sys_permission_set` row: the `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` promotion, `auto-org-admin-grant.ts` (walled and `single`), `plugin-auth/auth-manager.ts` self-registration, `verify/src/rls.ts`, and the Setup user page's Add picker (`linkField: 'permission_set'`, `valueField: 'name'`). Pinned on databases holding zero `sys_permission_set` rows: `grant-permission-set-name.writers.test.ts`, `auto-org-admin-grant.test.ts`, `grant-permission-set-name.test.ts`, `plugin-auth/audience-posture.test.ts`, `verify/rls-persona-grant.test.ts`. The repository's own fixtures (dogfood, cli, rest, hono-server, sharing, organizations) were moved to the name.
2. "`permission_set_id` stops being required, and nothing writes or derives from it any more" — **met.** `required: false`; no writer fills it; `grant-permission-set-name.ts` no longer derives the name from it; `last-admin-guard` and `delegated-admin-gate` judge the name. What still reads the id does so only to restrict (the one-time backfill, the D10 reference report, bootstrap leg C, the org-admin revoke / superseded-variant / duplicate reach, the uninstall reach), each labelled for C7b. That is D10's own order: mirrors and the column go after the rewrite is verified, never before.
3. "the Setup grant picker lists the security catalog" — **not met on this head**, by the dev's own account: the picker writes the name but still lists `sys_permission_set` rows, because objectui's related-list Add picker reads object records only. Seat answer 6110777865 moved this sentence to E2 (C9 part 3, measure-only, on objectui#7611) and rules that 6b-2-pre lands with the picker on rows, which exist until 6b-2. The gap is owned and gates 6b-2's landing, not this PR's; this record does not fail on it.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong:

1. `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`: `required: false, readonly: true` → `required: true`, writable. Narrowing for every caller: an id-only write is now refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `required` (pinned for a non-system and a system writer). Widening for non-system callers: the name is now theirs to supply. **Right** — D4, "every reference names it by its machine name".
2. `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set_id`: `required: true` → `required: false`, relabelled "Permission Set (legacy id)"; the `Field.lookup('sys_permission_set')` declaration stays. Widening (an id-less write lands). **Right** for this stage; the lookup's target retires in stage 8, where E3 → A turns the field into `Field.text` — not here.
3. New write-time refusal: a non-system insert, or an update that changes `permission_set`, naming a set the bound security catalog does not hold → `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `reference_not_found` at `permission_set`, `constraint { target: 'permission', targetField: 'name' }`. It replaces the former `invalid_value` mismatch envelope (and its `constraint.derivedFrom`). Narrowing on the value domain, in the envelope `sys_user_position.position` already answers with. **Right** — one dialect for "this reference names nothing", no new error code (ADR-0112 / ADR-0114). A deactivated set is still accepted and switched off by the activation ledger, not the write door — right under D3.
4. System writes are no longer judged against the catalog (the former derivation refused a disagreeing name from system writers too). Widening for `isSystem` only; stored as written, confers nothing until the name resolves. **Right** — the seed-ordering stand-down the engine's own lookup refusal takes; declared in the changeset and in census row 23c.
5. A catalog read that throws refuses nothing: the write proceeds and the operator is told at `warn` (pinned). The former hook refused on a thrown read. Widening in a degraded state only: no grant confers through a name that resolves nowhere (D4 fails closed at resolution; the D10 reference report names it at boot). **Right**, with one note: the changeset text does not say it. Not a failure — pinned, logged, inert for authorization.
6. `plugin-auth/last-admin-guard.ts`: `permission_set_id` / `permissionSetId` leave `GRANT_STANDING_KEYS`; `simulatedGrantSetName` is deleted. A write re-pointing the sole administrator's grant by id is no longer refused 403 (pinned: "writing the legacy id moves no standing"); re-naming it by `permission_set` is still refused (pinned). Widening, **right**: nothing derives standing from the id any more.
7. `delegated-admin-gate.directGrantSet`: an insert or a re-name is judged by the written name against the catalog; no `loadSetRowById` on this path. **Right.**
8. `auto-org-admin-grant.ts`: `resolvePermissionSetId` (the per-organization row resolution, its cache and its refusal warning) is deleted; the grant is written by name once `orgAdminSetMissingFromCatalog` (reading `securityCatalogReaderOf(ql)`) answers. Behaviour change: under a wall an organization with no own `sys_permission_set` copy is now **granted** where it was `skipped` / `permission_set_missing`; the skip survives only when the bound catalog lacks the set, and a new `reason: 'catalog_unreadable'` (a new value on the result) covers a catalog read that throws. `backfillOrgAdminGrants` no longer returns early on zero rows. The duplicate check reaches a legacy unnamed grant only through a row the backfill would name it by (organization-less or the organization's own); a legacy grant on another organization's copy is left and the pair is granted by name — one conferring row, pinned. **Right** under D3 / D4; this widening is the stage's purpose.
9. `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`: the promotion writes the name; `findExistingPlatformAdmin` reads by name with leg C off (`adminPsId` undefined); `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` keeps `admin_permission_set_missing` (the set is not shipped) and `admin_permission_set_unreadable` (the row table did not answer, so leg C cannot ask — no promotion). **Right**, pinned with every `sys_permission_set` row deleted afterwards. Unchanged here, correctly: the `single` grant still carries `organization_id: null`; D5's Default-Organization ownership is another stage's sentence, not this one's.
10. `cleanup-package-permissions.ts`: revokes grants naming the set plus legacy grants by the set row's id, de-duplicated by row id. **Right** — uninstall still revokes (the cli integration test pins it).
11. `verify/src/rls.ts`: no row read; the "boot seeded no row" refusal is gone, the "catalog does not serve the set" refusal stays. **Right.**
12. `platform-objects/pages/sys-user.page.ts`: list column `permission_set` (the id column leaves the list), picker `valueField: 'name'`, `linkField: 'permission_set'`, still `object: 'sys_permission_set'`. **Right** as far as objectstack metadata reaches (sentence 3 above).
13. Exports: plugin-security's `grantSetNameMismatchMessage` / `grantSetNameMismatchError` are removed and `grantSetNotInCatalogMessage` / `grantSetNotInCatalogError` added; `registerGrantPermissionSetNameHooks(engine, logger?)` gains an optional parameter; plugin-auth's `grant-set-name.ts` drops `GRANT_SET_ID_FIELD` (its header: internal, not re-exported). No `index.ts` is in the file list, so no package entry changes; the plugin-security `minor` covers its removals either way.
14. Object metadata: `titleFormat`, `highlightFields` and the `display_title` formula read `permission_set`; the generated translations (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES) are rewritten for both columns and no longer describe the retired derivation. **Right.**
15. Docs and skill: `permission-sets.mdx` grants by name; `system-context.mdx` row 23c is rewritten and the census counts move 122 → 123 (the hooks' new `session.isSystem` read); `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` prescribes `permission_set` by name and calls `permission_set_id` legacy. **Right**; the skill edit is what makes the PR Tier H, as the dev reports.
16. Not changed, correctly: no index change, no DDL, no data rewrite, no boot migration — D10 keeps every one of those for the operator ceremony (C7b). The declared unique index still keys `permission_set_id` (③ Q4).

ADR-0131 reading: this is D10's first step as the seat named it — every writer references the set by name (D4); the write door and the writers consult the registry-backed catalog and nothing else (D4, "resolution reads the registry"); nothing is deleted or constrained before the rewrite is verified (D10 fate 2's gate). None of §8's inherited rules is touched: no driver arm, no default owner, no deletion, no merged two-source list, no edit under `content/docs/releases/`.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/15204-grant-by-name-security.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` **minor**, BREAKING named, with before / now / unchanged / remedy paragraphs and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Matches the diff: the accept-set change is on a platform object's data rows (two declared fields flip required / optional and a value-domain refusal is added), not on any spec schema key, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite and no tombstone; the existing one-time backfill and the id column's later drop are the migration story it names. **Right.**
- `.changeset/15204-grant-by-name-writers.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/verify`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` **patch**, one sentence each that matches its diff (self-registration by name with no row read and the guard reading the name alone; the probe persona no longer needing a row; the picker writing the name while still listing rows). **Right** under the repository's launch-window convention as `Check Changeset` (green on this head) reads it. One reading for the seat: plugin-auth's `GRANT_STANDING_KEYS` loses two members and a formerly-403 write now lands — declared in the changeset text, a loosening that confers nothing; `patch` is defensible and the gate accepts it.
- The PR body's Clause-② declaration reads `yes (narrowing)`, the one spelling for a diff that widens one surface and narrows another (`clause2-line.mjs`), which is exactly ① rows 1–6: narrowing on the data door (the name is required and must be in the catalog), widening on the id column, the system stand-down and the standing keys. **Right**, and it matches the `minor` + BREAKING changeset. The expectation in 6109520247 ("a required field becomes optional") names the widening half; the arm names the breaking half the gates must see.
- Noted, not failed: the catalog-unreadable stand-down (① row 5) is absent from the changeset text.
- Size: 2,693 changed lines, under the 3,000 line (`Check PR Size` green).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6110797712, `open_questions`, each answered:

1. The grant picker still lists `sys_permission_set` rows → **A, and already escalated**: 6110777865 sends it to C9 part 3 (objectui#7611, measure-only, including the spec-18 pin question); 6b-2's landing is gated on E2 or a maintainer ruling; this PR lands as built. The position picker shares the gap (the dev's third out-of-scope finding) and rides the same measure.
2. The restrict-only legacy-id reaches (backfill, D10 report, leg C, org-admin revoke / superseded / duplicate, uninstall) → **A, keep them until C7b.** Each one only restricts; deleting them now opens the second-platform-admin and standing-`organization_admin` windows on an upgraded database's first boot; D10 sanctions the deletion only after the verified rewrite; #22601 B forbids conferring fallbacks, and none of these confers.
3. Refuse a written `permission_set_id` now? → **A, leave it inert.** The name is required, so an id-only write already fails loudly; an id beside a name is read by nothing that grants; a refusal for a column C7b drops is a one-stage gate. Carried to C7b: the unique index still keys the id, so a stray id written beside a name is the one way a by-name grant can still collide in the database — harmless, and it goes with the column.
4. The by-name unique key → **A, with C7b.** Until then the database does not refuse two by-name grants of one set to one user in one organization from the data door (the platform writers check by name first). Grants are additive, so a duplicate confers nothing extra; the ceremony dedupes before it constrains, and an index added here would fail on live data this stage is barred from rewriting.

PR body acceptance notes: uniqueness (= Q4). Pre-ADR-0113 databases with a `NOT NULL` `permission_set_id` → accepted: recorded as not measured to exist, and the drift report's `relax_not_null` names the remedy for an operator who meets one. Writing `permission_set_id` not refused (= Q3). Translations rewritten → verified in the diff, four locales.

`out_of_scope_findings`: the junction `sys_position_permission_set.permission_set_id` and its writers → stage 8 (the junction object retires there; E3 → A covers the user-grant lookup); the `component.zod.ts` TSDoc naming `relationshipField=permission_set_id` → prose only, stage 8 or the next spec toucher; the position picker → E2. All three are already carried on the card; nothing new to file.

`deviations`: (1) `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` edited → Tier H; the shipped text was falsified by the diff and now matches it — right to edit, maintainer approval owed. (2) Docs and fixtures outside the landing zone → each a producer this change falsified; right. (3) Spec not regenerated → right, the mention is prose. (4) `label-write` no-op → nothing to judge. (5) Footer form → nothing to judge. (6) PR body "236 files green" against the report's 235 passed + 1 skipped + 11 red, then fixed → a body figure the seat may correct; the record does not turn on it.

Not in this stage (PR body): `suggested-audience-bindings.ts` (U2, #22854) untouched — U2 writes the junction, not a user grant; the dev's merged-tree dogfood run covered its acceptance suite, and the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` (all three shards green, below) is the gate of record.

One pin removed and not replaced: an unrelated update to a legacy unnamed grant (name `NULL`, before the backfill) through the engine is no longer pinned to land without naming it; the object comment says it does ("an update that leaves the column alone does not have to name it"). Not a contract change this PR makes; noted for the backfill's own tests.

**Gates on this head**, read at render time. Completed and green: Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3, 2/3, 3/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core (6/6), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace, filter. Skipped by design: Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in). **Still pending at render time:** Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (5/6). Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; the queue holds the landing on them and this record does not stand in for them. Nothing on the head is red.
